syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

concepts.learning_objective: Define a map as a selective, symbolised and generalised representation of the earth at a reduced scale.
Distinguish a map from a sketch on the basis of scale and orientation.
Explain why scale and map projection are the first essentials of map making.
Explain map generalisation as selecting and simplifying content for the map's purpose.
Describe map design and map construction and production as steps of cartography.
Recall the early contributions of Mesopotamia, the Greeks and the Arabs to map making.
Trace the development of map making in India from the Vedic period to the Survey of India.

topics.title: Types of maps based on scale
topics.ncert_sections: Types of Maps Based on Scale

concepts.learning_objective: Identify cadastral and topographical maps as large-scale maps and state their purposes.
Identify wall maps and atlas maps as small-scale maps and compare their scales.

topics.title: Types of maps based on function
topics.ncert_sections: Types of Maps Based on Function

concepts.learning_objective: Identify relief, geological, climatic and soil maps as physical maps.
Identify political, population, economic and transportation maps as cultural maps.

topics.title: Uses of maps: measuring distance, direction and area

concepts.learning_objective: Choose suitable methods to measure straight and zigzag distances on a map.
Explain how directions are determined from the north base line using cardinal points.
Calculate area on a map using the method of squares and describe the polar planimeter.

topics.title: What is Scale and Systems of Measurement

concepts.learning_objective: Explain map scale as the ratio between map distance and the corresponding ground distance.
Recall the units of the Metric and English systems of measurement and convert between them.

topics.title: Statement of Scale and Graphical Scale

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the statement of scale method with its advantages and limitations.
Explain why the graphical or bar scale stays valid when a map is reduced or enlarged.
Interpret a representative fraction as a ratio of map distance to ground distance in the same units.
Explain why the representative fraction is the universal method of scale.
Convert a statement of scale into a representative fraction.
Convert a representative fraction into a statement of scale in a given system.
Calculate the length of line and divisions needed to construct a graphical scale.
Apply the angled-line method to divide an uneven line into equal parts.

topics.title: Shape of the Earth and the Geographical Grid

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the earth is described as an oblate spheroid rather than a perfect sphere.
Describe how the poles provide reference points for a grid of parallels and meridians that acts as geographical coordinates.
Define latitude and state the values and number of parallels at one-degree intervals.
Interpret how the length of a degree of latitude varies slightly between the equator and the poles.
Describe the steps for drawing a parallel of latitude on a circle using a protractor.
State the properties of meridians and the role of the Prime Meridian at Greenwich.
Explain how meridians are drawn as seen from above the North Pole, with east and west reversed.
Compare parallels of latitude with meridians of longitude in shape, length and spacing.
Calculate local time from longitude using the rate of 4 minutes per degree.
Explain the choice of a standard meridian and how Indian Standard Time is derived from 82 degrees 30 minutes E.
Explain why the date changes on crossing the International Date Line near the 180 degree meridian.

topics.title: Map projection and the need for it
topics.ncert_sections: Map Projection; Need for Map Projection

concepts.learning_objective: Define map projection and graticule and explain the limitations of a globe.
Explain why projections are needed and why distortion is inevitable on a flat surface.
Describe the reduced earth as a model drawn to a reduced scale.
Distinguish parallels of latitude from meridians of longitude.
Identify the four global properties a projection tries to preserve.

topics.title: Classification by drawing technique and developable surface

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish perspective, non-perspective and mathematical projections.
Classify projections as cylindrical, conical or zenithal and as normal, oblique or polar.

topics.title: Classification by global properties and source of light

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish equal area, orthomorphic, azimuthal and equi-distant projections.
Classify gnomonic, stereographic and orthographic projections by the position of the light.

topics.title: Conical projection with one standard parallel

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the reduced-earth radius and choose the standard parallel and central meridian for a conical projection.
State the properties, limitations and uses of the simple conical projection.
Calculate the radius, equator length and interval for a cylindrical equal area projection.
State the properties, limitations and uses of the cylindrical equal area projection.
Explain the orthomorphic properties and rhumb lines of Mercator's projection.
Evaluate the limitations and uses of Mercator's projection.
Describe topographical maps as large-scale general purpose base maps prepared by the national mapping organisation.
Relate the scales of Survey of India topographical maps to their latitudinal and longitudinal coverage.

topics.title: Methods of relief representation and contours

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the methods used to show relief on maps, such as hachures, hill shading, layer tints, spot heights and contours.
Explain contour interval, horizontal equivalent and the basic features of contour lines.
Distinguish gentle, steep, concave and convex slopes from the spacing of contours.

topics.title: Landforms shown by contours
topics.ncert_sections: Types of Landform; Valley; Cliff; Waterfall and Rapids

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise conical hills, plateaus, cliffs and waterfalls from their contour patterns.
Distinguish V-shaped valleys, U-shaped valleys, gorges and spurs on a contour map.
Apply the steps for drawing a cross-section from contours using a suitable vertical scale.

topics.title: Cultural features and map interpretation
topics.ncert_sections: Identification of Cultural Features; Interpretation of Topographical Maps; Map Interpretation Procedure

concepts.learning_objective: Identify settlement types, sites and transport patterns shown on topographical sheets.
Interpret a topographical sheet under its standard heads and by superimposing feature maps.

topics.title: Meaning and stages of remote sensing

concepts.learning_objective: Define remote sensing and identify its three basic components.
Sequence the stages of remote sensing data acquisition from energy source to map.
Identify the regions of the electromagnetic spectrum used in remote sensing.
Explain why different objects respond differently in different spectral regions.
Describe how atmospheric constituents absorb and scatter reflected energy.

topics.title: Remote sensing satellites and data reception

concepts.learning_objective: Compare sun-synchronous and geostationary satellites by altitude, coverage, resolution and use.
Describe how image data is received, corrected and converted into maps.
Distinguish photographic and non-photographic sensors.
Describe the working of a whiskbroom scanner.
Explain and calculate the detector array of a pushbroom scanner.

topics.title: Resolving powers and sensor resolutions
topics.ncert_sections: Resolving Powers of the Satellites; Sensor Resolutions; Table 6.1

concepts.learning_objective: Explain temporal resolution and its use in change detection.
Distinguish spatial, spectral and radiometric resolution using Table 6.1.
Distinguish images from photographs and describe photographic images.
Explain pixels and digital numbers in a digital image.
Classify elements of visual interpretation into image and terrain characteristics.
Interpret tones and colours of features on a standard false colour composite.
Apply texture, size, shape, shadow and pattern to identify features.
